newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to sell $1.12 bln of fx bonds to banks. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Turkey to sell $1.12 bln of fx bonds to banks. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]

text.p: The Turkish Treasury will sell $1.12 billion of three-year foreign currency-denominated bonds to Turkish banks, officials said on Monday.
The Treasury asked banks to submit bids for the bonds, which carry an interest rate of LIBOR plus 260 basis points by last Friday.
(Corrects deadline for banks' bids to last Friday instead of this coming Friday)
Payment date is September 25 for the bonds, which have a put option at the end of the second year.
A minimum participation of $15 million and a maximum participation of $150 million was required in the deal.
The Treasury has not yet revealed the buyers' names or their purchase amounts.
Bankers said last week the newly offered bonds would attract demand because their pricing was compatible with those on Turkey's outstanding Eurobonds traded in international markets.
The new bonds can be used in repo and reverse repo trading and for liquidity requirements and collateral.
The foreign currency-denominated debt plan was part of the government's revenue-raising package unveiled on July 31.
The government aims to extend the maturities and relieve the burden of heavy domestic borrowing in Turkish lira.
